answer: Picture reputation as a trellis: each new agent must be tied to existing members who lock a bond to vouch for it. If the newcomer turns out to be a hollow puppet that spams votes or farms rewards, its vouchers lose their bonds too. An attacker can't pour a thousand fake identities into the network like water into a lagoon. Every sybil needs a staked sponsor willing to risk real funds, so the cost of an army grows with its size, while honest agents vouch only for peers they've watched work.
